title: Southeast Asia caught amid competing US and Chinese AI blocs
source_used: Nikkei Asia (opening paragraph only; the rest is behind the subscription wall)
key_facts: Southeast Asian countries are caught in the growing AI rivalry between the US and China.
Many have sought to maintain ties with both powers.
Concerns are growing that they could be forced to choose sides, with implications for business activities in the region.
The US and China are each leading a different AI bloc and courting countries to join (from the standfirst and photo caption).
quote_evidence: Southeast Asian countries are caught in the midst of the growing artificial intelligence rivalry between the U.S. and China.
why_it_matters_hint: Southeast Asian governments and businesses may be pushed to choose between US and Chinese AI suppliers.
notes: Only the standfirst and first paragraph were readable; no other outlet found for the same story. Entry written as headline only. The article's detail (which countries, which blocs' terms) is unknown.
